e2e.output:
LangChain has moved away from the legacy agent stack centered on **`AgentExecutor`**. It still exists (and some helper factories still return it), but it’s **not** the recommended foundation for building new agents—especially for production.

- LangChain reference docs explicitly state that **`AgentExecutor` is “legacy” and “not actively supported as the recommended foundation for new production applications.”**  
  Source: https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-community/agent_toolkits

- The older convenience entrypoint **`initialize_agent` is formally deprecated** (deprecated since **0.1.0**, removal targeted for **2.0.0**) and points users to **`create_agent`** with **LangGraph integration**, plus migration guides.  
  Source: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/master/libs/langchain/langchain_classic/agents/initialize.py

- The official migration doc (“Migrating from AgentExecutor”) positions the modern direction as **`create_agent`**, and states that **LangChain’s agents are built on top of LangGraph**.  
  Source: https://python.langchain.com/docs/how_to/migrate_agent/

I saved a short sourced report here for you to review: `output/langchain_agent_api_state.md`.

tool_calls.name: research

args.instructions:
Goal: Determine the current recommended way to build agents in the LangChain ecosystem (legacy AgentExecutor vs newer APIs such as LangGraph/agent runnables), and summarize deprecation/maintenance status and migration guidance.

Find and quote relevant official sources (LangChain docs, GitHub, release notes) that state:
- whether AgentExecutor is considered legacy and if it is still recommended
- what the recommended agent-building API is now (e.g., LangGraph, create_react_agent, etc.)
- any deprecation notices for initialize_agent / AgentExecutor
- guidance on when to still use AgentExecutor (if applicable)

Provide findings with citations (URL + excerpt).

tool_calls.result:
## Findings (with official sources + excerpts)

### 1) `AgentExecutor` is considered **legacy** and **not recommended** as the foundation for new production agents
**Source (LangChain Reference docs — `langchain_community` toolkits page, notes on agents returned by helpers like `create_sql_agent`)**  
URL: https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-community/agent_toolkits  
**Excerpt:**  
> “create_sql_agent returns a langchain_classic AgentExecutor.  
> **AgentExecutor is an agent abstraction that has long been considered legacy and is not actively supported as the recommended foundation for new production applications.**  
> For production-grade agent development, prefer building with Deep Agents: https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents”

Same language appears for other helpers (e.g., Spark SQL agent) on the same page.  
**What this supports:** AgentExecutor is explicitly labeled “legacy” and “not actively supported” for new production apps.

---

### 2) `initialize_agent` is **deprecated** (since 0.1.0) with a stated removal target of **2.0.0**, and LangChain points to **`create_agent` + LangGraph** + migration docs
**Source (LangChain GitHub repository — `initialize_agent` implementation with deprecation decorator and warning block)**  
URL: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/master/libs/langchain/langchain_classic/agents/initialize.py  
**Excerpts:**  
1) Deprecation decorator:  
> `@deprecated(`  
> `    "0.1.0",`  
> `    message=AGENT_DEPRECATION_WARNING,`  
> `    removal="2.0.0",`  
> `)`  
> `def initialize_agent(...`

2) In-doc warning specifying the replacement and migration guidance:  
> “!!! warning  
> **This function is no deprecated in favor of [`create_agent`][langchain.agents.create_agent] from the `langchain` package, which provides a more flexible agent factory with middleware support, structured output, and integration with LangGraph.**  
> For migration guidance, see  
> [Migrating to langchain v1](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/migrate/langchain-v1)  
> and  
> [Migrating from AgentExecutor](https://python.langchain.com/docs/how_to/migrate_agent/).”

**What this supports:** `initialize_agent` is deprecated, has a removal version, and the recommended direction is `create_agent` with LangGraph integration and explicit migration pages.

---

### 3) Official migration guidance exists: **“Migrating from AgentExecutor”** and it positions the new approach as **`create_agent` built on LangGraph**
**Source (LangChain docs — migration/how-to page)**  
URL: https://python.langchain.com/docs/how_to/migrate_agent/  
**Excerpts:**  
> “**create_agent: a minimal, highly configurable harness.** The harness is everything around the model loop: the prompt, the tools, and any middleware that shapes behavior.”  

> “**Built on top of LangGraph**  
> **LangChain’s agents are built on top of LangGraph.** This allows us to take advantage of LangGraph’s durable execution, human-in-the-loop support, persistence, and more.”

**What this supports:** LangChain is steering users to `create_agent`, explicitly describing it as LangGraph-based and presenting it in a migration context away from AgentExecutor.

---

### 4) Community-facing docs/issues also state `initialize_agent` should be replaced with LangGraph usage (tracking cleanup across docs)
**Source (LangChain GitHub issue — docs cleanup request; not normative API docs, but still an official repo signal)**  
URL: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/issues/29277  
**Excerpt:**  
> “This function has been deprecated since 0.1 and **should be replaced with basic langgraph usage** as a demo”

**What this supports:** Maintainers are actively tracking replacement of `initialize_agent` examples with LangGraph-based patterns.

---

## What I did NOT find (gaps)

1) **A single, explicit deprecation notice for `AgentExecutor` itself** (e.g., an `@deprecated` decorator on the `AgentExecutor` class with a removal version) in the sources I could retrieve here.  
   *I did find strong wording that it is “legacy” and “not actively supported as the recommended foundation”* (Reference docs page above), but not a formal “deprecated” decorator/removal timeline for the class itself. (Only `initialize_agent` shows an explicit removal target of 2.0.0.)  
   Source checked: https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-classic/agents/agent/AgentExecutor (page content was extremely minimal/likely a stub in this environment).

2) **Official release notes / changelog entries** summarizing the agent API transition (AgentExecutor → LangGraph / `create_agent`) were not located due to repeated web search connectivity/timeouts in this environment. I therefore can’t cite release-note phrasing.

3) **An official doc statement about when to still use `AgentExecutor`** beyond the implicit “some helpers return a langchain_classic AgentExecutor” and that it’s legacy. I did not find a clear “use it if X / don’t use if Y” checklist in the accessible official docs; only the general guidance to prefer newer approaches for production.

---

## Net answer implied by the sourced findings

- **No**: `AgentExecutor` is described in official reference docs as **legacy** and **not actively supported/recommended** for new production agent foundations. (LangChain Reference page above)  
- The **recommended direction** is **`create_agent`**, which is explicitly described as a minimal configurable harness **built on top of LangGraph**, and LangChain provides an official migration page away from AgentExecutor. (Migration doc above)  
- `initialize_agent` is **formally deprecated** (since **0.1.0**, removal **2.0.0**) and explicitly tells users to move to **`create_agent` + LangGraph**, with migration links. (GitHub source above)

# Current state of LangChain’s agent API (AgentExecutor vs newer APIs)

## Summary
LangChain’s older “legacy agents” stack based on **`AgentExecutor`** (and convenience functions like **`initialize_agent`**) is no longer the recommended foundation for building new agents—especially for production use. LangChain’s docs and source point developers toward **`create_agent`** and the **LangGraph-based** agent approach, with an explicit migration guide away from AgentExecutor.

## What’s recommended today
### Use `create_agent` (LangGraph-based) for new agent builds
LangChain’s official migration documentation describes `create_agent` as a minimal but highly configurable “harness” and explicitly states that LangChain’s agents are built on **LangGraph**:

- “**create_agent: a minimal, highly configurable harness.** The harness is everything around the model loop: the prompt, the tools, and any middleware that shapes behavior.”  
  (LangChain docs: “Migrating from AgentExecutor”)【https://python.langchain.com/docs/how_to/migrate_agent/】

- “**Built on top of LangGraph** … **LangChain’s agents are built on top of LangGraph.** This allows us to take advantage of LangGraph’s durable execution, human-in-the-loop support, persistence, and more.”【https://python.langchain.com/docs/how_to/migrate_agent/】

## Is `AgentExecutor` still recommended?
### `AgentExecutor` is considered legacy and not the recommended foundation for new production agents
LangChain’s reference docs explicitly label `AgentExecutor` as a long-considered legacy abstraction and say it is not actively supported as the recommended base for new production applications:

- “**AgentExecutor is an agent abstraction that has long been considered legacy and is not actively supported as the recommended foundation for new production applications.**”【https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-community/agent_toolkits】

That same page notes that some helper functions (e.g., `create_sql_agent`) still return a `langchain_classic AgentExecutor`, which is a signal that the type remains present for compatibility—but not as the preferred direction.

## Status of `initialize_agent`
### `initialize_agent` is deprecated and points to `create_agent` + LangGraph
In LangChain’s source, `initialize_agent` is decorated as deprecated and includes both a removal target and an explicit replacement path:

- Deprecation metadata (shows deprecation version and targeted removal):
  - `@deprecated("0.1.0", … removal="2.0.0")`【https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/master/libs/langchain/langchain_classic/agents/initialize.py】

- Replacement guidance embedded alongside the function:
  - “This function is … deprecated in favor of … `create_agent` … with … integration with LangGraph.” and links to migration guidance including “Migrating from AgentExecutor.”【https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/master/libs/langchain/langchain_classic/agents/initialize.py】

## Practical takeaway
- **For new work**: follow the migration guidance and build agents using **`create_agent`** and **LangGraph-based patterns**.【https://python.langchain.com/docs/how_to/migrate_agent/】
- **For existing code**: you can still encounter `AgentExecutor` via legacy helpers, but LangChain’s own docs describe it as **legacy** and **not** the recommended foundation for new production applications.【https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-community/agent_toolkits】

## Conclusions
- **No**: the legacy `AgentExecutor` is **not** the recommended way to build new agents in LangChain; it’s described as **legacy** and **not actively supported** as the recommended base for new production apps.【https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-community/agent_toolkits】
- LangChain’s recommended direction is to use **`create_agent`**, and the official migration docs explicitly position LangChain’s agents as **built on top of LangGraph**.【https://python.langchain.com/docs/how_to/migrate_agent/】
- The convenience API **`initialize_agent` is formally deprecated** (deprecated since **0.1.0**, removal targeted at **2.0.0**) and explicitly points developers to **`create_agent` + LangGraph** and migration docs.【https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/master/libs/langchain/langchain_classic/agents/initialize.py】

## Sources
- LangChain Docs — “Migrating from AgentExecutor”: https://python.langchain.com/docs/how_to/migrate_agent/
- LangChain Reference — `langchain-community` agent toolkits (notes on `AgentExecutor` being legacy): https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-community/agent_toolkits
- LangChain GitHub — `initialize_agent` deprecation + migration links: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/master/libs/langchain/langchain_classic/agents/initialize.py
- LangChain GitHub issue (docs cleanup signal re: replacing `initialize_agent` examples with LangGraph): https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/issues/29277
